structured_output.what_is_happening: FUNKOS is named after funkos.fun, a real but very small product ("pump.fun, but for AI agents": AI agents launch and trade pump.fun coins). I found no official token on the site, in its skill file or in the GitHub repo. This contract was deployed through uxento and migrated to PumpSwap at 14:31 UTC. The 1-minute GeckoTerminal candles show a bot pattern, not organic trading: a steady staircase of about $1.4-1.6k volume per minute pushing price up about 4% per minute, cut twice by large single-candle dumps. The first dump, at about 14:45, took price from 1.21e-3 to 2.5e-4. The price then laddered back to 7.85e-4, and a second dump pair at 15:07-15:09 took it to 6.7e-5, below the post-launch level. The detection trigger (m5 -90%) was that final dump. In the last candles price is flat at about 7.7e-5. The near-identical unique buyer and seller counts (about 2,570 and 2,546) and RugCheck's "high holder correlation" warning fit a many-wallet volume and ladder bot.

narrative.description: AI agents launching and trading pump.fun coins (funkos.fun), a timely sub-theme next to pump.fun's own AI agent features (Mayhem Mode, tokenized agents). The product exists: a live website, a skill.md file and a GitHub repo with 0 stars. It is tiny and does not endorse any token.
narrative.why_spreading: The attention looks manufactured. About 10+ same-name FUNKOS tokens were launched over the prior ~10 hours, most now at zero liquidity. That is the typical pattern of trench bots copying a new dev tool's launch. The volume on this pair is a mechanical per-minute bot ladder, not organic buying.

token_connection.why_this_token: It uses the project's name, description and X handle (funkosfun) in its metadata. But the project does not name any official CA, and GMGN says the linked X account is attached to 95 token launches, so the metadata is easy to copy.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 10 other FUNKOS/funkos tokens were created earlier today. Most are dead with 0 liquidity, including HbgD... which shows a stale $13.5M mcap. BDKC...funk is still live with about $30k liquidity.

authenticity.evidence: GeckoTerminal 1-minute candles show a constant ~$1.5k/min staircase rising about 4% per minute, ended by giant dump candles ($28.6k, $21.8k and $14k volume). Unique buyers and sellers are almost equal. RugCheck warns of high holder correlation. The top holders each hold an identical 0.04%. GMGN puts the top entrapment-trader share at 0.77. There are no smart or renowned wallets and no calls.
authenticity.uncertainty: I could not see X posts (x.com returned 402). The ladder bot could restart for a third cycle, which would lift price quickly.

structural_risks: The operator has dumped twice. The price is now about 94% below ATH and near launch levels, which suggests the operator has exited.
The volume is bot-generated. If the ladder stops, the pair goes dead.
Many same-name copycats split whatever real attention exists.
The LP is burned, so a classic pull is unlikely, but a 'died' outcome through volume collapse is likely.

structured_output.counterargument: The ladder bot has already run two cycles: 6.7e-4 to 1.2e-3 in about 14 minutes, then 2.5e-4 to 7.85e-4 in about 21 minutes. If it starts a third cycle from about 7.7e-5, a 2x would take only about 18 minutes at the same pace, well before a -50% stop. Liquidity ($23k) is still healthy and the LP is burned. The funkos.fun product is real and fits the AI-agents-on-pump.fun theme.
unknowns: Whether @funkosfun endorsed any CA (X was inaccessible)
The identity of the dumping wallets and how much supply they still hold

source_coverage.notes: funkos.fun, skill.md and the GitHub repo name no token. The contract search returned nothing. x.com returned HTTP 402. The candle data came from the GeckoTerminal API, and a live check on DexScreener confirmed the metrics.

structured_output.thesis: This is a copycat token on a real but tiny AI-agent product, pumped by a mechanical ladder bot and dumped twice. The price now sits near launch level after the operator's exit dump. A 2x needs the bot to restart, and I have no evidence it will. The more likely outcome is that volume fades and the pair dies.
